integrity: The complete 1994 same-object paper was inspected through the exact map equation, one-sided coexisting-attractor geometry, and attractor-merging crisis, with full-document searches for moment, average, invariant-measure, covariance, and mean formulations. The 1979 source date and strange-attractor lineage were verified independently, and the later stochastic Holmes-map literature was checked for stronger statistical coverage. The invariant cubic moment law, Cauchy-Schwarz mean-variance envelope, equality classification, reflection symmetry, and periodic sign-side consequence were reconstructed independently. The algebra and classical parameter specialization were replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The sharp mean-variance envelope requires invariant support in one closed diagonal quadrant and is not asserted after a sign-spanning attractor merger.
The theorem constrains low moments but does not identify the invariant distribution or prove existence of a chaotic attractor.

The historical 1979 source concerns the underlying Duffing oscillator and its Poincare dynamics; the complete equation-level cubic-map comparison is the 1994 same-object paper that attributes the map to Holmes.
The 2004 stochastic-stability paper was compared through accessible scientific material rather than complete full text.
An equivalent short moment identity could remain in unindexed map literature.
title: Sharp one-sided stationary moment envelope for the Holmes cubic map
